title: Initial functional mapper
summary: Established the first usable DirectInput-to-vJoy application shell for Battlefield 6.
highlights: Qt Quick application shell and persistent configuration model.
DirectInput physical-controller acquisition and vJoy virtual output worker.
Initial four-axis routing intended for roll, pitch, throttle, and yaw.
Basic mapping start/stop behavior and first-pass controller/vJoy status.

title: Diagnostics and vJoy stabilization
summary: Made the first mapper easier to diagnose and more tolerant of real vJoy installation layouts.
highlights: Improved vJoy readiness and capability reporting.
Automatic location/loading of the installed vJoy interface path.
Expanded live diagnostics for controller and virtual output state.
Safer output reset behavior during stop/disconnect paths.

title: Per-axis configuration
summary: Moved mapping from a simple global setup toward profile-ready, per-axis control.
highlights: Dedicated Axes workspace and selected-axis workflow.
Per-axis route, deadzone, hysteresis, inversion, and output-limit controls.
Live curve preview tied to the selected physical axis.
Persistent axis selection and richer input/output instrumentation.

title: Axes workspace and live visualization
summary: Completed the richer axes workspace foundation and improved live transform visibility.
highlights: Separate physical-input and transformed-output markers.
Dual input/output response visualization.
More complete axis status/instrumentation.
UI refinements preparing the curve editor and profile-aware processing pipeline.

title: Advanced response curve studio
summary: Turned response shaping into a full editor rather than a handful of static curve choices.
highlights: Linear, J-Curve, and S-Curve families with multiple strengths.
Advanced evidence-informed presets and Personal Presets.
Point-based editing with Smooth/Linear interpolation and multiple point densities.
Large response graph, live markers, gain/reference views, comparison/audition tools, and signal-path display.
Immutable 4097-sample compiled lookup tables kept runtime curve evaluation fast.

title: Profiles and physical profile controls
summary: Added instant profile switching and runtime Hold/Toggle controls without burdening the mapping loop.
highlights: Persistent Normal/Precision-style profiles with create, clone, rename, delete, and activation.
Physical-button Profile Hold and Profile Toggle behavior.
Deterministic Hold → Toggle → manual base-profile precedence.
Profile switches compile complete mapping state before worker adoption.
Stop/disconnect clears runtime-only profile overrides safely.

title: Installer, launcher, and automatic updates
summary: Converted the project from a development executable into an installable application with a stable release pipeline.
highlights: Native Win32 launcher and stable-release automatic update checks.
Single HOTAS_VERSION authority across app, launcher, installer, and release manifest.
Per-user Inno Setup installer with Start Menu/Desktop shortcuts.
GitHub Actions build, test, benchmark, packaging, checksum, manifest, and installer smoke pipeline.
Optional Authenticode signing hooks.

title: POV diagnostics and profile controls
summary: Brought physical POV hats into diagnostics and the same profile-control model used by buttons.
highlights: Support for up to four physical POV hats with raw values and logical directions.
Eight logical direction cards per hat.
POV direction Profile Hold/Toggle controls.
Expanded bounded event log and POV diagnostics.
Safer center/disconnect behavior for newly exposed hat state.

title: Native vJoy POV and dependency bootstrap
summary: Added direct POV-to-vJoy routing and made the installer more helpful around required controller dependencies.
highlights: Native continuous/discrete vJoy POV passthrough independent of direction-as-button routing.
POV direction profile controls retained alongside native hat output.
Improved axis Output Min/Max controls and selector behavior.
Installer detection/offering of pinned vJoy and HidHide dependencies when missing.
Application icon package integrated across mapper, launcher, installer, and shortcuts.

title: POV, profile-control, and UI stabilization
summary: Polished the v1.6 input stack into a stable visual and behavioral baseline.
highlights: Resolved native POV target parsing and profile-trigger schema issues.
Kept native hat output and direction routing visibly separate.
Improved dark selector/popup consistency and control presentation.
Strengthened icon/resource and dependency validation in CI.
Established the presentation later preserved as the Legacy theme.

title: Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun themes
summary: Separated presentation from mapping and added three persistent visual systems.
highlights: Legacy preserves the v1.6.3 interface, Standard provides the modern general UI, and Top Gun adds the aviation treatment.
Theme state persists separately from profiles and mapper configuration.
Top Gun adds naval-instrument surfaces, fighter artwork, wing badge, technical lines/stripes, aviation typography, and themed footer/header details.
Theme switching remains UI-only and does not touch DirectInput, vJoy, mapping state, or profile semantics.

title: Deterministic Automation engine
summary: Added a compiled Automation subsystem while preserving the mapper-first performance architecture.
highlights: Up to 64 rules with up to four conditions and four actions each.
Axis, button, POV, profile, and Always conditions with explicit matching behavior.
vJoy Button Hold/Toggle, Profile Hold/Toggle, and bounded axis Scale/Offset/Clamp/Override/Mix/Follow actions.
Persisted master kill switch, invalid-rule health, and Automation diagnostics.
Automation compiles to fixed-capacity worker records before report processing.

title: Stabilization and update awareness
summary: Addressed axis parking safety, profile creation polish, and in-app update visibility.
highlights: Global Disabled Axis Value setting from -100.0% to +100.0%, defaulting to 0.0%.
New Profile dialog restyled across all themes and Start From selector fixed.
Profile creation deep-copies the chosen source profile.
Asynchronous in-app stable-update awareness with top-bar and Settings handoff to the launcher.

title: Full-page Automation editor
summary: Replaced the modal-style Automation editing experience with a dedicated, safer rule workspace.
highlights: Each Automation opens in a full-page editor.
New rules are persisted as disabled, incomplete drafts with no default side effects.
UI-only draft state validates before Save Automation persists and compiles the rule.
General, WHEN, THEN, priority, enabled state, deletion, and unsaved-change handling moved into one coherent editor.
Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun share the same Automation behavior.

title: Human-readable Automation rule builder
summary: Reworked Automation around user-facing intent instead of engine terminology.
highlights: WHEN SHOULD THIS HAPPEN? and WHAT SHOULD IT DO? builders.
Plain-language requirement/effect summaries and readable profile names.
All the time as a user-level rule choice, with legacy Always normalization hidden underneath.
Consistent AND/OR connectors for multi-requirement rules.
Live RULE SUMMARY and Advanced-only priority controls.

title: Temporal Automation triggers and controls
summary: Expanded Automation from state matching into event, sequence, and timed behavior.
highlights: Button pressed/released events, two-to-five press sequences, and long-press triggers.
Axis crosses-above/crosses-below events with hysteresis.
Momentary, whole-rule Toggle, and Timed rule behavior.
Bounded Tap virtual button action with worker-owned expiry state.
Advanced timing for sequence gap, long press, brief active duration, and tap duration.
Runtime latch/timer state clears on stop, disconnect, configuration replacement, and master disable.

title: Axis safety, mapping controls, and extended routing
summary: Closed the major BF6 hardware-use gaps with explicit mapping-state controls, axis domains, richer labels, and wider vJoy routing.
highlights: Physical-button and Automation Mapping On, Mapping Off, and Toggle Mapping controls.
Mapping Off centers axes, releases buttons, centers POVs, and keeps the physical/vJoy devices acquired.
Reconnect seeds a fresh physical snapshot to prevent artificial input edges.
Centered/One-Sided axis domains stored per profile.
Per-profile custom physical axis/button names and game-facing vJoy output aliases.
Runtime discovery of X/Y/Z/Rx/Ry/Rz/Slider 0/Slider 1 virtual axes.
Direct decimal Output Min/Max entry with 0.1% step controls.
Disabled/unsupported outputs are parked without stale commands while the fixed-array hot path is preserved.

title: Public readiness and automatic controller setup
summary: Makes first-run controller setup substantially clearer through an explicit, transactional vJoy/HidHide readiness workflow while preserving the mapper's deterministic real-time architecture.
highlights: First-run Controller Setup wizard and persistent Settings entry for Detect → Explain → Fix → Verify → Ready.
Pure capability planner computes virtual axes, buttons, and native POV requirements from profiles and Automation, with deterministic CI tests and mocked process transactions.
Supported vJoyConfig integration snapshots Device 1, preserves known FFB state, changes only an insufficient target after explicit approval, verifies the result, and rolls back on failure.
Supported HidHideCLI integration allowlists HOTAS BF6 before hiding only the exact selected HID instance, preserves unrelated rules, verifies cloaking, and supports narrow session undo.
Mapping is explicitly Off, neutralized, and released before setup changes; setup never runs in the DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
Adds normal development CI, MIT licensing, third-party notices, structured hardware compatibility documentation, and conservative BF6/anticheat guidance.

title: HOTAS Setup & Verification correctness update
summary: Corrects false readiness warnings and makes setup verification clear, passive at startup, and safe to run while preserving mapper performance.
highlights: Renames the feature to HOTAS Setup & Verification and removes the first-run setup modal from healthy startup.
Recognizes HOTAS BF6's own vJoy Device 1 acquisition as Ready while retaining a distinct external-owner conflict state.
Uses active DirectInput report evidence and the exact DIPROP_GUIDANDPATH HID identity already captured by the mapper.
Adds passive asynchronous startup checks plus visibly-progressing, user-requested full verification.
Restores the exact prior Mapping On/Off choice after full verification or a scoped automatic repair.
Presents one shared verification model through Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun visual systems.

title: Automatic repair verification and single-UAC flow
summary: Makes the scoped Automatic HOTAS Repair path cohesive, diagnosable, and authoritative without changing the mapper runtime.
highlights: Replaces the default-looking automatic-repair confirmation with a shared themed overlay for Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun.
Builds the exact approved vJoy/HidHide repair plan before one elevated transaction, including in-transaction rollback for partial failures.
Captures per-operation start, completion, exit-code, standard-output, and standard-error diagnostics without exposing raw command dumps in normal UI.
Distinguishes administrator cancellation, command failure, verified Ready, and completed-but-inconclusive Attention results.
Normalizes and uses the exact selected HID instance for HidHide changes while preserving unrelated device and application entries.
Runs bounded post-repair verification and restores the prior Mapping On/Off state outside the real-time report path.

title: Real-world setup and calibration reliability
summary: Targets the remaining external-machine setup failures without changing the real-time mapper architecture.
highlights: Controller arrival evaluates readiness and opens the shared setup dialog only when selection, calibration, vJoy, HidHide, or another action needs attention.
Two-stage range then robust center calibration makes measured neutral the user-facing 0.0% for centered axes while retaining range-only controls.
Axis meters and linear graphs consume calibrated coordinates; raw sensor readings remain explicit Diagnostics data.
Automatic HidHide setup requires a forced DirectInput reacquisition and fresh physical report before Ready is published.
A failed physical reacquisition triggers narrow transaction rollback and clear reconnect/rollback status instead of stranding the selected controller.
Attention and failure states include Copy Diagnostics with sanitized setup, repair, rollback, and calibration evidence.
